itemUsage.en: Leontuzzo, ex-heir to Famiglia Bellone, simply a Siracusan citizen these days.
itemUsage.zh: 前贝洛内家族少爷，莱昂图索，如今只是叙拉古的一介普通市民。

itemDesc.en: With the waves he's stirred, he's pessimistic about getting the last laugh. He's not giving up, though, never.
itemDesc.zh: 他对能否在自己掀起的浪潮中笑到最后持悲观态度，但他并不打算放弃。

Operator Vigil has demonstrated a remarkable aptitude in the designation of tactical points for summoning reinforcements so as to secure leeway for deployment.
The Field Operations Department has thus passed the following resolution:
This operator shall be appointed a Vanguard Operator during field operations to exercise Tactician responsibilities.
In witness whereof,
This badge is hereby conferred upon the above named.

description.en:
The shoe-shiner trembles as he enters the Bellone famiglia parlor.
He trembles not because this is Bellone territory. He had shined Bernardo's shoes for thirty years, and the man always respected those who respected him. The last time he had stepped into this parlor, it was so that he could offer Bernardo the chance to name his son.
His fear comes from the fact that the one sitting here today is not Bernardo, but his son, Leontuzzo.
He has not heard much about the Bellone heir. All he knew was that the young master had never come to him for a shoe shining.
'My father isn't here at the moment, but you can trust me as you trusted him.'
His words calm him a bit, allowing the shoe-shiner to explain why he had no choice but to come:
His son leads a decent, honorable life, and fell in love with a lady from Columbia. However, that lady was also being pursued by a maniac who didn't take kindly to a rival. Three nights ago, his son was cornered by that maniac and beaten within an inch of his life. He'd sought aid from the courts, but the man belonged to a Columbian famiglia, and his lawyers were easily able to secure a 'not guilty.'
'When I was leaving the courtroom, he stepped in front of me and shoved two banknotes into my pocket. He laughed as he told me it was for my son's medical fees. I...' The shoe-shiner went on, tears streaming from his wizened eyes.
Leontuzzo listens in silence. He knows that if his father were here, he would surely give the old man a pat on the shoulder, acknowledge his suffering, then provide a solution to this. A humane way.
Generally speaking, these things could only be resolved with bloodshed.
But that was not how he does things.
'What is it you wish for, signor?'
'I have no requests, Don Leontuzzo, other than justice for my boy.'
'Justice. Am I to understand that you want this man to feel the same pain your son did?'
'That's right. Nothing more.'
Leontuzzo snaps his fingers, and a red-headed young man steps out from a door to the side.
'Demetri, go investigate the gang behind that guy first.'
'Easy enough, but what comes next?'
'Next... If I'm not mistaken, those Columbian gangs want to sidestep us and cozy up to the local government. Then let's propose sending local 'talents' to the Columbian frontier. Hopefully, every famiglia will enthusiastically agree. Let them send off a few stronzi who should have been exiled long ago.'
The red-headed youth snaps his fingers. 'So we'll ship this guy off too?'
'Exactly.'
'Capisco.'
With that final declaration, the man leaves the room. Leontuzzo turns towards the astonished shoe-shiner. 'This is the justice I can give you. Are you satisfied with it, signor?'
The shoe-shiner quickly catches on, and his gaze turns from astonishment to gratitude.
'Take this.'
'This is...'
'My pistola. Place it by your shoe-shiner, and nobody will cause you trouble.'
'But—'
'Don't worry. I barely use it. Whenever you feel like you can sleep easy again, just give it back to the guard downstairs.'
description.zh:
擦鞋匠战战兢兢地走进了贝洛内家族的会客室。
他的战战兢兢并不来自于这里是贝洛内家族的领地，他为老贝纳尔多擦了三十年的皮鞋，而老贝纳尔多总是乐于尊重那些尊重他的人，上次他踏入这里的时候，是来请老贝纳尔多为他的儿子命名。
他的惶恐来自于今天坐在房间里的，并不是老贝纳尔多，而是他的儿子，莱昂图索。
他没怎么听说过这位少爷的消息，他只知道，这位少爷从来没有去他那里擦过鞋。
“我的父亲暂时不在，但是，你可以像信任他一样信任我。”
青年的话仿佛带着一种魔力，让擦鞋匠悬着的心稍微放下了一些，开始讲述他不得不来到这里的理由——
他那做正经生意的儿子，和一位来自哥伦比亚的女子相爱，可是那名女子有一个蛮不讲理的追求者，对方不忿于他儿子的存在，在三天前的夜晚，堵住了他的儿子，将他打成重伤。他试图寻求法院的帮助，然而，对方属于来自哥伦比亚的某个家族，请的律师轻而易举地将一切罪责洗得干干净净。
“当我走出法院的时候，那人走到我的面前，塞给我两张钱，笑嘻嘻地告诉我这些钱拿去当我儿子的医药费。我……”擦鞋匠说着说着，眼泪从干枯的眼眶中汹涌而出。
莱昂图索静静地听着，他知道如果他的父亲在这里，一定会拍拍老擦鞋匠的肩膀，安抚他，对他的痛苦表示尊重，然后给出一个充满人情味的解决方法。
一般来说，解决方法无非是见一些血。
但他不会这么做。
“您想要什么？”
“我没有别的要求，尊敬的莱昂图索，我只希望能够伸张正义。”
“正义。我可以理解为，您希望他们承受和您儿子相同的痛苦吗？”
“是的，我别无他求。”
莱昂图索打了一个响指，一个红发的青年应声从侧门走出。
“德米特，先去调查清楚那人背后的帮派。”
“这个简单，但是然后呢？”
“然后，如果我没记错的话，那些哥伦比亚帮派想要绕开我们和本地政府打好关系。那就让我们的人提出一份法案，内容是给哥伦比亚拓荒区输送‘人才’，希望各家族积极相应。我们就挑几个本来就要流放的家伙进去。”
红发青年打了个响指，“然后，把这个人加进去？”
“没错。”
“明白了。”
青年说着就离开了房间，莱昂图索则转向有些错愕的擦鞋匠，“这是我为您准备的正义，不知道您是否满意？”
擦鞋匠很快理解了其中的奥秘，看向莱昂图索的目光从错愕变成了感激。
“对了，拿着这个。”
“这是……”
“我的‘铳’，把它放在您的擦鞋机器边上，这样就不会有人来找您麻烦了。”
“但是——”
“放心，我很少用到它，在您觉得能睡安稳觉的时候，再把它交给楼下的门卫就好。”

description.en: Leontuzzo is somewhat nervous in the driver's seat. Today is the first time he's officially driving a car. Look both ways. Adjust the seat. Adjust the rear-view mirror. Fasten the seatbelt. Check the gear. Once all these steps are complete, he looks at the passenger seat with some trepidation. Lavinia sits there, his instructor for the day. Only once she nods does he let out a faint sigh of relief, turn the key, and start the engine. The car slowly trundles out the garage and onto the street. The streets are, as always, showered in a patter of drizzle. Leontuzzo flicks the windshield wipers, taking care to keep his foot on the brake, and not daring to go too fast. 'You're driving far too slowly, Leon. You'll never learn anything like that.' Her role as driving instructor has not given her cause to loosen her usual strictness. 'The more you remind me, the more nervous I get, Lavinia.' Leontuzzo has a death grip on the steering wheel, his eyes locked onto the road ahead, refusing to turn his head even an inch. 'Who was it at breakfast who was so excited to show off his skills to Demetri once he got back?' 'I let the steam from the bread get to my head.' As they speak, the car reaches an intersection. Just as the red lights are about to go green, several pedestrians cross. However, the moment they see the emblem atop the oncoming car, they immediately lower their heads and hurry down the rest of the crosswalk. Unfortunately for one of them, they trip and fall as they do so. Lavinia looks at Leontuzzo, as if asking him: 'What should you do in this situation?' '...I should slam the accelerator and run the red light. Best to give them a splash and a little scare.' But even as he says this, he presses down on the brake, letting the car slowly come to a stop in front of the crosswalk. The fallen pedestrian clambers back to their feet, giving the two in the car a slight nod of thanks before quickly leaving the scene. 'If most famiglia members drove like you, I'd be able to shave off a tenth of the cases I preside over each year, if only for minor incidents like just now.' Lavinia speaks with approval of his action. 'Honestly, there are simply too many traffic laws. I'm not keen on remembering them all either.' The light turns green, and Leontuzzo restarts the car. 'But there's one thing I've come to realize lately. We follow these so-called laws not because they are natural to us, but because they are self-evident principles we as a people discover as we seek justice.' 'Well said, Leon. It seems you have a thorough understanding of those traffic laws after all. Now let's see if you can actually remember them.' 'Oddio, Lavinia, are you seriously going to give a lecture here?' 'I did promise your father to teach you everything I know. So, Leon, what are those white lines by the side of the car meant to indicate?' 'Wait, give me some time to think...' The rains of Siracusa are endless and suffocating, but at the very least, inside this car, the warmth of chatter can be felt.
description.zh:
主驾驶席上，莱昂图索有些紧张，今天是他第一次正式开车上路。
观察左右，调整座椅，调整后视镜，系好安全带，确认档位——完成了这些步骤后，他有些忐忑地看向副驾驶席，那里坐着拉维妮娅，他的教练。直到拉维妮娅点了点头，他才微微松了口气，然后，扭动钥匙，启动引擎。车辆缓缓离开车库，驶入街道。
街上一如既往地下着淅沥的小雨，莱昂图索打开雨刷器，小心地踩着踏板，不敢开得太快。
“莱昂，你开得太慢了，这样练习是没什么效果的。”拉维妮娅作为他学车的教官，对他一如既往地严格。
“你越是提醒我，我越是紧张，拉维妮娅。”莱昂图索紧握着方向盘，认真盯着眼前的道路，甚至连头也没有侧一下。
“是谁今早在餐桌上兴致勃勃地说等德米特里回来，要给他露一手？”
“那是我被面包的热气蒸坏了脑袋。”
说话间，车开到了一个十字路口前，前方的红灯即将转绿，人行道上，几个行人正在通行。然而，几个行人似乎是看到了驶来的车辆上面的标志，立刻低下头，快步走过人行道。
不幸的是，其中一个人走到一半，绊了一跤，摔倒在人行道上。
这时，拉维妮娅看向莱昂图索，眼神像是在问：“现在，你的正确做法是什么？”
“……我该狠狠踩下踏板，冲过红灯。最好溅起一阵水花，把行人吓一跳。”
嘴上这么说着，莱昂图索却放缓了车速，车缓缓停在了人行道前。
摔倒的人此时也爬了起来，向车内的两人微微点头表示感谢之后，快步离开。
拉维妮娅有些欣慰地开口：“如果大部分家族的人能像你一样开车——哪怕只是刚才这点微不足道的事情，我每年要判的案子恐怕都能少十分之一。”
“那些交通规则太繁琐了，老实说，我也不想去记。”绿灯亮起，莱昂图索重新启动了车辆，“不过，我最近越来越理解一件事，我们之所以遵守所谓的规则，并不是因为它们天然存在，而是因为，它们是人们追求公平的过程中发现的不言自明的道理。”
“你说得很不错，莱昂。看来，你对交通规则已经有了非常深入的理解，现在，让我看看你是不是真的记住了。”
“天哪，拉维妮娅，你在这里也要教书吗？”
“毕竟，我答应了你父亲，把我知道的一切都教给你。所以，莱昂，现在汽车侧边这些白线的作用是什么？”
“等等，让我回忆一下……”
叙拉古的雨季总是漫长且沉默，不过至少，此时车内的谈笑声能够让人获得一丝温暖。
